pronunciation.approximation: Say "wamani" with the stress and length implied by the scholarly restoration "Wamani".
pronunciation.note: The ASCII form "wamani" is a DNS compromise; the restoration "Wamani" preserves the name's scholarly dignity.

domains.title: Wamani
domains.subtitle: Sacred Mountain
domains.lead: Wamani is sacred mountain. The name means "The falcon" and belongs to the incan tradition.

cards.name: Sacred Name
cards.desc: The restoration Wamani returns the figure to scholarly recognition.

cards.name: Living Tradition
cards.desc: Honored in incan myth, cult, and cultural memory.

symbols.name: Name
symbols.meaning: The restored form Wamani, carrying scholarly and cultural weight.

mythology.lead: The stories of Wamani place sacred mountain at the center of a living mythological world.

myths.title: Origins
myths.text: Wamani appears in incan tradition as sacred mountain. The name's meaning, "The falcon", shapes the narratives told about this figure.

myths.title: Worship and Memory
myths.text: Devotees and later tradition-keepers preserved Wamani in ritual, text, and iconography, ensuring the name survived into the modern scholarly record.

lore.culturalLegacy: Wamani remains a touchstone for understanding incan religion, art, and identity.
scholarlySources: Bauer, Brian S., The Sacred Landscape of the Inca (1998).
Moseley, Michael E., The Incas and Their Ancestors (2001).
